method: Pinned blob verified then untruncated first500 source lines read. Remaining implementation receives no whole-file credit.
findings: Header identifies noncryptographic XXH32/64 and XXH3 64/128 families. Hash equality alone is not byte equality; performance table describes historical i7-9700K/Ubuntu20.04/clang10 setup and is not current local measurement.
API overview permits null input only for zero length and requires readable input range; C++ byte access requires trivially-copyable objects. Implementation-specific null behavior remains unread.

Streaming lifecycle requires create/reset/update/digest/free; digest documented as nonmutating and updates may continue afterward. XXH3 state allocation/alignment must use dedicated allocator rather than arbitrary malloc/new.

Documented FILE example stops on fread returning0 but does not inspect ferror, and ignores reset/update/free statuses. It is an illustrative snippet, not evidence of production rmlint IO handling; copying it unmodified could finalize a truncated read.
Canonical output mandates big-endian representation instead of dumping host-endian integer bytes. This is relevant to portable cache/result persistence and distinct from in-memory comparison.

Inline/private mode enables internal state, emits private API and undefines/remaps symbols/types under XXH_INLINE_ to handle prior noninline includes. Namespace prefixing avoids symbol collisions; static internal-state ABI is explicitly unsuitable for dynamic linking.
